title: Preview URLs (per-version-id + stable alias) and production URL are distinct addressable surfaces; the promote step is what changes which one production maps to
context: The failure mode this ADR closes is the collapsed URL: a project where the reviewer of a merged change and the visitor to the deployed application look at the same URL. When the preview surface and the production surface are the same string, every merge is a production act, review is what happens after users notice, and rollback is a second merge landing before enough users notice. The vendor's own primitive shape supports keeping them distinct: every uploaded version has a permanent per-version-id URL and a mutable stable-alias URL that can be pointed at the newest-of-main; production is the mapped custom domain (or the workers.dev production host) whose current version id changes only on an explicit deploy verb.
decision: The blueprint mandates three URL kinds per Worker, all distinct hostnames, all discoverable through the Deploy Adapter's `deploy status` verb: (1) a per-VERSION-ID URL, unique per upload, permanent, useful for pinning a change-review link; (2) a STABLE PREVIEW ALIAS URL fixed to an operator-chosen alias string (the common default is `main`), always resolving to the newest-of-main uploaded version, useful for a persistent stakeholder-shareable link; (3) a PRODUCTION URL, declared under the wrangler manifest's `route`/`routes`/`workers_dev`/custom-domain stanza, changing which version it maps to only when a `promote` workflow runs. The Preview URL Resolver (TAC-1303) assembles the first two and refuses any alias string whose assembled host segment equals the production URL's host segment. The manifest loader refuses a wrangler config whose production route resolves to the preview alias URL host with `DEPLOY_URL_COLLAPSED`.
consequences: Reviewers and stakeholders reach the newest-of-main at a persistent, memorable URL that never masquerades as production. Users hit production at a hostname that only changes version behind an explicit operator act. Change-review links are pinnable to a specific version id and never rot. The trade is one Worker now surfaces three URLs the project has to reason about (and the operator has to explain once when a new engineer joins); the payoff is the class of leaks-through-collapsed-URL is closed by the manifest's own validation, not by discipline.

alternativesConsidered.name: Preview alias URL and production URL as the same string with a query parameter switching mode
alternativesConsidered.summary: One hostname, `?preview=1` flips to the newest-of-main; production is the default response.
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: The query-parameter mode is trivially forgettable and does not survive a link-shortener, an email quoting, or a browser that strips query strings. The class of leak this ADR closes reopens exactly when the operator hands out the URL to someone who does not add the query parameter.

alternativesConsidered.name: Per-version URLs only; no stable alias URL
alternativesConsidered.summary: Every upload gets a URL; the stable-shareable-review-URL story is 'copy the URL from the CI run'.
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: The per-version-id URL is essential for pinning a change; the stable alias URL is essential for a persistent 'the latest' surface stakeholders can bookmark. Shipping only the first fails the persistent-review use case; the vendor's own primitive supports both cheaply so both ship.

alternativesConsidered.name: Preview URL = production URL under a special header
alternativesConsidered.summary: One hostname; the vendor routes to the newest-of-main when a specific request header is set (a signed cookie, an auth-only bypass).
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: Same class as the query-parameter option: the mode is invisible to the URL string and non-portable across link handoffs. It also couples the preview surface to an auth model that may not exist on day one.
